records.title: bug(analytics): pv_* materializations hardcode org depth; sector goes NULL once territory is inserted
records.body:
Part of #855. **Blocks #923.**

Not one of the epic's originally-catalogued breakages — found while re-reviewing the open child issues on 2026-09-12. `apps/analytics` landed in #800, after the audit that produced #855, so its SQL was never in the tree that was audited. It is the same failure shape as the rest of this epic: a fixed number of hops that returns quietly wrong results instead of erroring.

## Why

The eight `pv_*` materializations ([`specs/analytics-parquet-etl.md`](https://github.com/F3-Nation/f3-nation/blob/main/specs/analytics-parquet-etl.md)) flatten the org hierarchy into one column pair per tier. Flattening is the one representation that genuinely cannot be depth-agnostic — a column per level *is* a hardcoded ladder — so the tier has to be added deliberately. Three files additionally assume the *current* depth and break beyond simply omitting territory.

### 1. `pv_events.sql` — sector falls off the end

[`org_chain`](https://github.com/F3-Nation/f3-nation/blob/main/apps/analytics/analytics/sql/pv_events.sql#L39-L41) joins exactly three parent hops:

```sql
FROM pg.public.orgs o
LEFT JOIN pg.public.orgs p1 ON p1.id = o.parent_id
LEFT JOIN pg.public.orgs p2 ON p2.id = p1.parent_id
LEFT JOIN pg.public.orgs p3 ON p3.id = p2.parent_id
```

Each tier is then picked out by `COALESCE(CASE WHEN o.org_type = '…' … p3.org_type = '…')` — see [`sector_org_id` at L30-33](https://github.com/F3-Nation/f3-nation/blob/main/apps/analytics/analytics/sql/pv_events.sql#L30-L37).

For an AO-hosted event today the chain is `o=ao, p1=region, p2=area, p3=sector`. It fits with nothing to spare. Insert territory and it becomes `o=ao, p1=region, p2=area, p3=territory` — **`sector_org_id` and `sector_name` go NULL on every event row.**

### 2. `pv_areas.sql` — the parent guard stops matching

[L7](https://github.com/F3-Nation/f3-nation/blob/main/apps/analytics/analytics/sql/pv_areas.sql#L7):

```sql
LEFT JOIN pg.public.orgs sector ON sector.id = area.parent_id AND sector.org_type = 'sector'
```

Once an area hangs off a territory, `area.parent_id` is a territory id and the `org_type = 'sector'` guard fails. **`sector_id` / `sector_name` go NULL for every migrated area** — and because the rollout is gradual, this degrades area by area rather than all at once, which is harder to spot.

### 3. `pv_sectors.sql` — areas stop being children

[L15](https://github.com/F3-Nation/f3-nation/blob/main/apps/analytics/analytics/sql/pv_sectors.sql#L15) builds each sector's area list from direct children:

```sql
WHERE a.org_type = 'area' AND a.parent_id = s.sector_id
```

Areas are no longer direct children of sectors, so this returns **zero areas per sector**.

## Blast radius

These are not internal: the Parquet output is published to GCS and read downstream — the spec notes "PAX Vault may read GCS directly." A sector page built on `sector_org_id` gets nothing, and any sector-level rollup silently reports zero. Because the job is a daily full refresh that treats a bad dataset as a normal failure only when it *errors*, a NULL-but-valid Parquet file publishes cleanly.

## What to build

- [ ] Replace the three fixed hops in `pv_events.sql` with a depth-agnostic ancestor walk (a recursive CTE — DuckDB supports `WITH RECURSIVE`), resolving each tier by `org_type` at any depth
- [ ] `pv_areas.sql`: resolve the area's sector by walking ancestors for `org_type = 'sector'` rather than checking the immediate parent, **and** add `territory_id` / `territory_name` alongside it
- [ ] `pv_sectors.sql`: count areas by ancestry rather than `parent_id` equality; add a territory list/count
- [ ] `pv_events.sql`: add `territory_org_id` / `territory_name` to the flattening
- [ ] Audit the other five (`pv_regions`, `pv_aos`, `pv_pax`, `pv_kotter`, `pv_upcoming`) for the same assumptions — `pv_aos` and `pv_regions` mention no sector today, but the check should be explicit rather than assumed
- [ ] Update `specs/analytics-parquet-etl.md` for any output-contract change; adding columns changes the published schema

**Every territory column must tolerate NULL.** The rollout is gradual, so an area with no territory is a permanent, legitimate state — not an anomaly to filter out.

## Ordering

This lands **before** #923, for the same reason the other traversal rewrites did: the ancestor-walking form can be proven to produce byte-identical output on today's five-tier data, so any later difference is unambiguously the new tier rather than the rewrite. Adding the territory columns can land in the same PR or a follow-up, since they are simply NULL until territories exist.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On today's five-tier data, all eight materializations produce output identical to the current implementation
- [ ] Against a six-tier fixture, `sector_org_id` is populated on events, `pv_areas` resolves the sector through the territory, and `pv_sectors` counts its areas
- [ ] Against a **mixed** fixture — one area under a territory, one still directly under its sector — both resolve correctly
- [ ] Territory columns are present and NULL-safe
- [ ] `specs/analytics-parquet-etl.md` matches the output contract

records.title: an Op that fans a change out downstream, in an order derived from the source
records.body:
## What

A change in one component fans out to everything downstream of it, in an order chant derives from the source rather than one anybody declares, dispatched through the Ops that already exist, behind a single gate.

Nothing drives this today. `chant run` deploys components with cross-stack output seeding, `resolveStackTargets` reads `ChantConfig.stacks[]` but only the lifecycle commands use it, and there is no path that takes "this changed" and turns it into "these run, in this order". The scale harness in `test/scale-estate.sh` loops one `chant run` per stack in the order a person wrote them down, which is a fair description of the problem rather than a solution to it.

## Why chant should derive it, not ask for it

The competing shape of this feature is a dependency registry: you declare, in a console or a config, that stack B depends on stack A. That registry is a second source of truth about a relationship the source already states, and it goes stale the first time someone adds an output reference without updating it.

chant does not need one. A child declares `stackOutput()` and a parent reads it through `nestedStack().outputs.name` (`lexicons/aws/src/nested-stack.ts`), and components seed each other's outputs at deploy time. The edge is a fact of the declaration. Deriving the order is a graph walk over something the build already holds.

That difference is the feature. A tool that makes you declare the order has relocated the problem.

## What already exists

Checked against the code before scoping, because an earlier draft of this issue named the wrong gap.

**Ordering is done, twice.** `resolveComponentGraph` (`packages/core/src/components/driver.ts:220`) takes components' `dependsOn`, Kahn-layers them into parallel-safe waves, flattens to a topological `order`, refuses a cycle with `DependencyCycleError` naming its members, and refuses a `dependsOn` it was not given with `UnknownDependencyError`. `computeStackGraph` (`packages/core/src/build.ts:68`) does the same over cross-lexicon stack edges and also returns `cycles`.

**Diamonds are done.** Kahn layering puts a component reachable by two paths in exactly one wave. This needs a test that pins it, not code.

**Change detection is done at stack granularity.** `lifecycle affected --base <ref>` (`packages/core/src/lifecycle/affected.ts`, CLI at `cli/handlers/lifecycle.ts:1869`) diffs built artifacts between two git refs and returns `changed` / `dependents` / `indeterminate`. Because it compares artifacts rather than file paths, a comment-only or refactor-with-no-output-change edit propagates to nothing. Its own module doc names this issue's gap: "This returns the set; it does not act. Fanning `lifecycle plan` / `ApplyOp` over it is an Op the user composes."

**Cross-component seeding is done.** `componentOutputs` threading in the driver, plus `--seed-outputs` / `--dump-outputs` on `chant run --components`, already carry one component's outputs into another's references across process boundaries.

## The actual gap

**1. Ordering a subset throws.** This is the load-bearing one, and it is the opposite shape from "we need a topological sort". Handing the driver the affected components alone fails, because a selected component still names a dependency that is not in the set:

```
✓ full set orders fine        → order ["net","cluster","app"], waves [["net"],["cluster"],["app"]]
✓ the affected subset throws  → UnknownDependencyError
```

A subset run needs the order derived from the **full** graph, execution restricted to the selected members, and the unselected dependencies' outputs seeded rather than recomputed.

**2. No component-level change signal.** `affected` speaks stacks; the driver speaks components. Nothing joins them.

**3. No gate over a set.** Gates are steps inside a component's own phases, so twenty components means twenty approvals.

**4. No resume.** `runInterpretDriver` stops the whole run at the first failed component, and a re-run redoes everything that already succeeded.

## Decisions

Recorded rather than left implicit, with the reasoning that settled each.

**The gate: one approval over the whole ordered set, bound to a digest of it.** #2300 is the precedent and the argument. It bound a gate's approval to the plan it approved, so a plan that digests differently is not what was approved and the run stops again. The same reasoning transfers: the approval names the fan-out that was derived, and a re-derived fan-out that differs is a different change. The digest covers the ordered selection, the edges it came from, and each component's input identity when the caller has one. It excludes the run id and the moment, per `lifecycle/plan-digest.ts`'s rules, so re-deriving an unchanged fan-out does not expire an approval on the clock.

**Partial failure: skip the subtree beneath the failure, continue independent branches.** Stopping everything is what the driver does today and it throws away the point of deriving the graph. The order came from the source, so a branch independent of the failure is known to be independent rather than assumed to be. Carrying on regardless is the unsafe option, because downstream of the failure is exactly where the changed value has not landed. Components beneath a failure record as `skipped` naming the failed ancestor, never `failed` — nothing about them failed, and that distinction is what makes the re-run legible.

**Precision: artifact diff, not file paths.** Reuse what `computeAffected` already does, which delivers "a change to a leaf propagates to nothing" with no new machinery.

**Indeterminate survives the join.** A component whose inputs arrive at deploy time cannot be judged from a source diff. One the walk reaches anyway is selected like any other dependent, because reachability is a fact about the graph rather than about whether the component's own inputs could be read. One the walk does not reach is reported, never decided in either direction. Fanning out to everything on an

records.title: fix(import): a same-thread parent cycle survives the guards and is written to the DB
records.body:
Deferred finding from the PR #118 review (the pre-existing `effectiveParent` pattern; the self-parent and cross-thread halves were fixed there in 0b33e45).

**What happens**

`runImport` builds `effectiveParent` in `src/lib/import/core.ts` (~799-808) and now skips a self-parent and a cross-thread pair. A same-thread cycle of two or more comments (A→B, B→A, both imported, same `thread_source_id`) passes both guards. `depthOf` (~815-838) terminates on the cycle via its `seen` set and assigns depth 1, but the UPDATE loop then writes both rows pointing at each other.

**Effect**

Roots are selected with `parent_id IS NULL` (`src/db/queries.ts:694`) and the recursive CTE walks from roots, so every comment in the cycle is counted in `new_comments` / `total_comments` and appears in RSS but never renders on any page. No error, no plan line.

**Scope**

Pre-existing core behaviour; affects all five adapters equally. Only reachable from a hand-edited export/DB — a well-formed source cannot produce a cycle — but every adapter walks untrusted input, which is why the other two shapes were moved into the core.

**Fix sketch**

Detect the cycle while building `effectiveParent` (or when `depthOf` bails) and re-root the cycle's members, counting them in the plan like the other re-rooted shapes. Tests belong next to the existing `parent guards` describe in `tests/import-core.test.ts`.

records.title: possible stack overflow in math parser
records.body:
* parse_unops can do basically infinite recursion (if you stick enough unary operators on an expression). to fix it we should probably add a recurseblock to it. (it's also possible to rewrite it using a manual stack instead but i'm not sure there's any point, given that the ast it generates will be highly recursive anyways.)
* math evaluation can do infinite recursion. this is trivial with recursive user functions (`function f(x) = f(x)`) but even without that, a pile of user functions where each function is a huge expression will still cause evaluation recursion depth to exceed the depth encountered when parsing. to fix this i guess we need to stick recurseblocks inside the implementation of every single math_ast node??

records.title: Core: Capture and organize durable text notes
records.body:
## Goal and value

Make Raphael usable as a Keep-like text-note app with areas, projects, active-project shortcuts, and favorites for frequently revisited areas, projects, and notes. This is the persistent manual foundation for the owner's eventual primary workflows: voice and image capture.

## Scope

Express, SQLite + FTS5, Drizzle, shared operation contracts, one shared API key, local server administration, remote mobile/CLI clients, immutable IDs and computed paths, canonical TipTap JSON with Markdown input/export, direct TipTap in a bundled react-native-webview, and Expo SQLite local drafts. Include hierarchy, text capture/editing, active projects, favorites, scoped search, moves, archive/restore, revisions, and creation idempotency. Creation and Get default to Markdown unless TipTap is explicitly selected. User API input uses operation-oriented POST endpoints and body selectors, not path/query addressing variants.

## Exclusions

Attachments, AI, voice/images, deployment/private access, general extension infrastructure, advanced metadata filtering, metadata patch editing in both clients, and conflict-resolution UI. Metadata storage remains supported. No root-level resources/projects or default inbox. Candidate epics are uncommitted and have no stories.

## Completion condition

From both mobile and CLI, the owner can create, retrieve, edit, find, organize, archive, and restore durable text notes within areas/projects. Active-project and favorite selections survive sessions. Both clients can favorite/unfavorite areas, projects, and notes and list full favorite nodes ordered by title then stable ID; mobile exposes Browse → Favorites. Favorites are independent of node revisions, survive moves/renames, and retain selection while effectively archived targets are hidden, reappearing when no archive cause remains. Data survives server/app restarts. Mobile-specific durable drafts and honest save/conflict outcomes are included; CLI need not reproduce mobile editing conveniences. Remaining platform/accessibility checks are implemented and verified rather than inferred from prototype success.

## Consequential decisions

- All sibling types share a slug namespace, including archived entities; collisions reject rather than auto-suffix.
- Mutations use revisions; creation uses client-generated idempotency keys. Conflict stops mobile autosave and preserves the draft; no merge/overwrite UI.
- New notes require explicit Save and parent selection. Containers created during capture commit independently of the draft.
- Editor starts with paragraphs, H1–H3, bulleted/numbered lists and list nesting. Existing supported code blocks remain editable; Mermaid stays source-only.
- Favorites use a separate backend-owned collection of stable node IDs and idempotent add/remove operations, without node revision changes. Ordinary node responses include derived isFavorite; a dedicated paginated API returns complete visible favorite nodes. The approved program design is preserved in #14.
- Active-project selection is explicit, independent of favorites/deadlines. Archive hides selected projects without clearing selection; restore makes them eligible again.
- Search covers title > plain description > derived body text; OR-default lexical syntax must be translated to FTS5. Default immediate children, explicit recursion, deduplicated scopes, type/kind/tag filters, skip 0 / limit 50 / cap 500, hasMore, no default total count. Archive inclusion arrives with lifecycle support.
- Keep the minimum internal built-in note-kind registration boundary; do not make a general extension framework a prerequisite.

## Sequencing and uncertainty

Implement hierarchy → capture → safe editing, then active projects/search/move, followed by complete archive lifecycle. Favorites (#14) build on node/note support and integrate the effective archive rules from #8. Existing stories #2–#8 remain unchanged. The user explicitly approved an eighth story as an exception to the five-story shaping budget, preferring the existing coherent boundaries over merges solely to meet a count. Scope is a bounded product promise, not every API discussed during architecture. Story details may be refined from evidence without discarding guarantees. Supported editor schema limits, asset hardening, production draft failure handling, and physical-device/accessibility verification remain implementation work; consequential newly discovered behavior returns to shaping.

## Spike findings and application

Two investigations were executed as isolated prototypes before issue creation; they are not retrospectively closed issue records.

Storage: Turso rewrite @tursodatabase/database 0.7.2 with Drizzle 1.0.0-rc.4 rejected recursive CTEs and required experimental Tantivy; direct FTS ordering was incorrect. User chose embedded operation over Postgres service and approved SQLite + FTS5 rather than closure-table complexity. Follow-up on macOS arm64/Node 26.8.1 tested better-sqlite3 13.0.3, drizzle-orm 0.45.2, drizzle-kit 0.31.10; 10 tests passed. Verified recursive scope + JSON + FTS, weighted ordering, skip/limit after deduplication, archive ancestry, revision CAS, idempotent create/outbox atomicity, transactional FTS updates/rollback, migrations, and WAL behavior. Drizzle expression-index generation failed; two partial unique indexes for root/non-root succeeded. These are tested versions, not mandatory future pins. Native installation elsewhere, load/lock handling, backup, and query translation remain unverified. SQLite is single-writer; keep transactions short. FTS uses custom virtual-table/trigger migrations. Public query semantics must not inherit FTS5's implicit AND accidentally.

Editor: direct TipTap 3.31.3 conversion/schema checks and offline bundling passed. MarkdownManager serialization preserved Mermaid arrows where a static-renderer experiment escaped them. Native Android host and then actual Expo 57.0.20 / RN 0.86.3 / react-native-webview 13.16.1 release APK were

records.title: [RTV-50-recursive-cte-repository] Recursive-CTE traversal repository (the concentration/nth-party query pattern)
records.body:
## Story

As a **Backend Developer**, I want a typed recursive-CTE traversal repository so that the concentration / sub-outsourcing-chain reachability queries — the product-defining operation — are proven on Postgres+Drizzle and ready for the domain engine to build on.

## Background

Parent epic **RTV-45** (#520). This is the exact query that decided Drizzle over Prisma: a
`WITH RECURSIVE` traversal that stays *typed* in Drizzle. It's the substrate for RTV-28 (arrangement
graph) and RTV-32 (change-impact materiality).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: A repository/query module exposing typed graph traversals via Drizzle `sql\`WITH RECURSIVE …\`` — e.g. `providerSubcontractorChain(providerId)` and `arrangementsReachingFunction(functionId)`.
- [ ] AC-2: Results are **typed rows** (not `any`/raw) — the traversal output has a declared shape.
- [ ] AC-3: **Cycle-safe** (guards against subcontractor cycles; bounded depth) and indexed for the traversal edges.
- [ ] AC-4: Integration tests (testcontainers) on a seeded chain: N-hop reachability returns the correct set; a cycle terminates.
- [ ] AC-5: A short doc/example in `retrieva/docs` showing the pattern (feeds RTV-28/32 + the RNCP "I own my SQL" evidence).

## Technical Notes

- Depends on tables existing (RTV-48) but is written generically over the graph edges so RTV-28's arrangement/provider/subcontractor tables plug in.
- Keep the SQL readable + commented — this is a defensibility artifact, not just code.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] ACs met; recursive traversal typed + cycle-safe + tested; doc example added; parent RTV-45 (#520) updated

## Dependencies
- Parent: #520 (RTV-45); Depends on RTV-48
- Feeds: RTV-28 (arrangement graph), RTV-32 (change-impact)

---
**Estimate:** 5 story points | **BMAD ID:** `RTV-50-recursive-cte-repository`

records.title: Examples of using `TreeNode` APIs to walk and manipulate LogicalPlans
records.body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem or challenge?

The usecase of walking `LogicalPlan` to either analyze the plan or rewrite it has come up multiple times recently

Specifically I think both @goldmedal  and @cisaacson  have asked about this recently and so I think the documentation is not clear enough





### Describe the solution you'd like

In order to help people do this, I would like to add some examples of how to walk the tree

I suggest first adding simple doc example in the [docs of `LogicalPlan` itself ](https://github.com/apache/datafusion/blob/b14e92f30057868da8e7b428223e66c6300773a1/datafusion/expr/src/logical_plan/plan.rs#L68-L69)

The example would do somethig like create a plan using `LogicalPlanBuilder` 
```
  Project
    Filter
     Scan
```

And then show how to:
1. Use `TreeNode::apply` to recursively find something about the scan (maybe the table name?)
2. Use the `TreeNode::rewrite` to recursively rewrite and remove the Filter (or something)

I think those would be relatively short examples to write and would illustrate the key apis







### Describe alternatives you've considered

Bonus points for a more full featured example (perhaps linked from the `LogicalPlan` docs) of how use / walk / manipulate LogicalPlans

Similarly to https://github.com/apache/datafusion/blob/main/datafusion-examples/examples/expr_api.rs, perahaps `datafusion-examples/examples/plan_walk.rs` or something

### Additional context

records.title: 🚀 Enhancement: Add Self-Relationship Support for Collections
records.body:
### 🔖 Enhancement description

Currently, Appwrite does not support self-referencing relationships within a collection. This feature request is to allow a collection to have a field that references itself, enabling hierarchical or recursive data structures.

### 🎤 Pitch

Self-referencing relationships are essential for various use cases, such as:  
- **Hierarchical Data:** Building structures like categories, threads, comments, or organizational hierarchies.  
- **Tree-Like Relationships:** Enabling parent-child relationships within the same collection (e.g., a category having subcategories).  
- **Graph-Based Models:** Creating complex interconnections within a dataset.  

**Example Implementation:**  
- Allow a document in a collection to reference another document within the same collection via a **"Self-Relationship"** field.  
- Provide validation to prevent circular dependencies if needed.  
- Enable querying/filtering based on these relationships to traverse hierarchical structures efficiently.  

### 👀 Have you spent some time to check if this issue has been raised before?

- [x] I checked and didn't find similar issue

### 🏢 Have you read the Code of Conduct?

- [x] I have read the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/appwrite/.github/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
